source_title: Uttarakhand to host 100-mile Himalayan Endurance Ultra Run from Mana Pass to Auli next May: CM Dhami - The Times of India
source_excerpt: DEHRADUN: Uttarakhand will organise a 100-mile Himalayan endurance ultra run in the first week of May next year, with the route passing through some of the stateâs high-altitude Himalayan destinations, Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami announced on Sunday.The proposed race will begin at Mana Pass, at an altitude of approximately 5,600 metres, and pass through Badrinath and Joshimath before concluding at Auli. Dhami made the announcement while participating in the Adi Kailash Parikrama Run 2.0 in Gunji, a remote border region of Pithoragarh district, as the state steps up efforts to promote adventure tourism.The chief minister felicitated the winners of the 70-km and 42-km races and encouraged runners who had arrived from different states. He said participating in competitions in the high Himalayas, amid challenging terrain, extreme weather conditions and low oxygen levels, reflects exceptional courage, discipline and determination.Dhami said the Adi Kailash Parikrama Run was more than a sporting event, describing it as a platform to showcase the natural beauty, cultural heritage and tourism potential of Uttarakhandâs border regions at the national and international levels.More than 700 runners participated in the eventâs inaugural edition in 2025, bringing attention to the adventure tourism potential of the Adi Kailash region. Dhami also noted an increase in the number of Inner Line Permits issued for the region compared with the previous year, indicating growing interest among tourists and pilgrims.The proposed 100 Miles Himalayan Endurance Ultra Run is expected to expand the stateâs long-distance endurance running calendar and attract participants from India and abroad. The government also expects the event to promote tourism in border areas and create employment and self-employment opportunities for local youth.Tourism and livelihoods in border villagesDhami said tourism could strengthen local economies and help address migration challenges in Uttarakhandâs border regions. Events such as the Adi Kailash Parikrama Run create business opportunities for homestay operators, local guides, transport providers, hotels and food businesses, he said.The government aims to ensure that tourism benefits reach local communities and support sustainable livelihoods.Referring to the Centreâs Vibrant Villages Programme, Dhami said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the approach towards border villages was shifting from viewing them as the countryâs last villages to recognising them as its first villages. Efforts are being made to improve infrastructure, promote tourism and expand livelihood opportunities in these strategically important areas.The state government is also promoting trekking, mountaineering, river rafting, kayaking, paragliding, mountain cycling and angling. An ultra-running event was organised in Niti Valley this year, while adventure tourism activities are being expanded in destinations such as Auli, Munsiyari, Rishikesh and Tehri.Dhami said Uttarakhandâs Himalayan geography, scenic landscapes and cultural heritage gave it a distinct advantage in adventure tourism. The government, he said, was committed to using this potential to boost the stateâs economy, generate employment and create sustainable livelihood opportunities.Traditional welcome in GunjiOn his arrival in Gunji, Dhami was welcomed by members of the Rang community dressed in traditional attire, showcasing the regionâs cultural traditions and heritage.He also acknowledged the contribution of the Indian Army, the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) and the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) to organising the event.
